reason: E1 shows a homogeneous BCC HEA with Tc ~7.5 K and intermediate electron–phonon coupling, supporting the link between BCC structure and superconductivity, but no cited evidence directly tests or supports the causal claims that configurational entropy drives homogeneity, that homogeneity optimizes coupling, or that reducing entropy degrades superconductivity.
premises: High configurational entropy stabilizes a homogeneous BCC lattice in HEAs
A homogeneous BCC lattice optimizes electron–phonon coupling
Optimized electron–phonon coupling enables conventional s-wave superconductivity with moderately high Tc
Reducing configurational entropy degrades lattice homogeneity and weakens electron–phonon interaction
Weakened electron–phonon interaction lowers Tc and reduces critical fields
